Windows release binaries are signed through SignPath. See the Code signing policy: https://amiberry.com/code-signing-policy

## Highlights

### Licensing and third-party code
- WHDLoad, JST and the Kickstart RTB files are no longer bundled. "Update WHDBooter files" and `--download-whdboot` now get them from their authors' sites:
  - WHDLoad comes from whdload.de on every update, so new WHDLoad releases arrive.
  - The SKick RTB files are fetched once, only while one is missing, from Aminet `util/boot/skick346.lha`. That archive is checked against a fixed SHA-256 before it is unpacked.
  - JST comes from Aminet `game/patch/jst.lha`, only when "Use JST instead of WHDLoad" is on.
  - `kick31034.A1000.RTB` is still bundled.
  - A downloaded file replaces the installed one only after it matches the size and CRC in its LhA header. Only one download runs at a time, and none starts while a machine is running unpaused.
  
  (#2540)
- If WHDLoad is missing when a WHDLoad game boots, Amiberry shows a message that says where to get it. Nothing is downloaded automatically. The Paths panel and the `--download-whdboot` help name the sources (#2540)
- In older releases, "Update WHDBooter files" now gets "not found" for the removed files. The installed copies are kept, and the update reports a partial failure (#2540, #2549)
- WHDBooter's quit-on-exit now uses `host-quit` from Host-Tools 2.8 (GPL-3) instead of AmiQuit, a third-party binary with no source or licence. host-quit also works on Kickstart 1.3 and the 68000 (#2549, #2550)
- LhA archives are now read with Lhasa 0.6.0 (ISC) instead of LHa for UNIX, whose licence is not free. The rare `-lh2-` and `-lh3-` compression methods are no longer decoded (#2558)
- Each LhA member's CRC is now checked, so a corrupt member fails instead of returning bad data. Truncated or corrupt archives fail cleanly; a corrupt `-lh5-`/`-lh6-`/`-lh7-` archive used to crash the old decoder. LhA's `0xff` path separators are read as `/` (#2540, #2558)
- PearPC was removed. It was never compiled into any build, so choosing it left the machine with no PPC at all. PPC emulation uses the QEMU plugin only. A configuration with `ppc_implementation=pearpc` loads as `auto` without a warning and is saved as `auto` (#2554)
- Licence clean-up:
  - The UAE portability headers and `vm.cpp` were rewritten under GPL-3.0-or-later, with no change in behaviour (#2552).
  - Third-party licence notices were corrected: HRTMon 2.37 is GPL-2.0-or-later, the Warp decruncher is LGPL-2.1-or-later, mos6502 is MIT (its source files now carry the notice) and iff.library is public domain. `gamecontrollerdb.txt` carries its zlib notice, unlzx credits all its authors, and Amiberry's copy of mt32emu is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later, as section 3 of the LGPL 2.1 allows (#2557).
- Each release now includes `amiberry-<tag>-third-party-sources.tar.xz`. It holds the exact source of the GPL and LGPL libraries bundled in the macOS release (such as FFmpeg, x264, x265, LAME, mpg123, libmpeg2 and libserialport), checked against Homebrew's checksums, and is listed in `SHA256SUMS` (#2556)
- The Amiga libraries some WHDLoad games need are no longer inside `boot-data.zip`, because their licences don't allow bundling them. "Update WHDBooter files" downloads them from their Aminet packages while one is missing; every file is checked against its CRC, and the packages that never change are also checked against a fixed SHA-256 (MMULib, which its author updates in place, isn't). ares_pc.releaseNotes:
ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

**NOTE**: The signing certificate used to sign ares on Windows has expired. ares will be unsigned until a compatible signing solution is found. **Sony - PlayStation**

 - Refactored core to use libco threading
 - CPU: implemented memory timing/control registers
 - CD-ROM: incorrect 150 LBA offset in command 0x14
 - CD-ROM: fix behavior when a command is issued before the previous has completed
 - CD-ROM: implement behavior where a new command cannot be executed until pending       
 - CD-ROM: implement 'command/parameter busy' register
 - DMA: improve chopping/allowing the cpu to run between blocks of a long transfer
 - DMA: fixed incorrect bit position for DMA channel chopping enable
 - DMA: fixed block DMA using incorrect timing
 - DMA: fixed SPU canReadDMA/canWriteDMA flags
 - MDEC: implement basic decode timing
 - MDEC: implement correct input fifo behavior
 - MDEC: fix behavior when an incomplete block is transferred via the input fifo
 - MDEC: fix DMA request registers, input/output full/empty registers, busy register
 - GPU: use correct clock frequency for PAL and NTSC
 - GPU: fix hblank timing
 - GPU: Fixed some clocking issues
 - Timer: improve behavior around timer overflow/target reached IRQ

**Nintendo - Game Boy Advance**

 - Only trigger keypad IRQ when input changes
 - Fixed handling of repeat bit during immediate DMA transfers
 - Prefetcher should fail reading across 128KiB boundaries
 - OBJ mosaic fixes to correct some graphical bugs
 - Prevent instruction tracing from modifying open bus
 - Refactored bus reads fixing some open bus edge cases
 - Implemented internal horizontal/vertical window flags when window boundaries reached
 - Improved affine parameter timings
 - Fixed wave RAM bank selection
 - Added OAM to memory viewer
 - Implemented OAM stage timings for sprite rendering

**Nintendo - Super Famicom / SNES**

 - Added support for loading GBC games in the Super Game Boy
 - Super Game Boy accuracy fixes (multiplayer, packet acknowledgement, register mirroring)
 - Improved auto-joypad polling accuracy

**Nintendo - Nintendo 64**

 - CPU & RSP JIT improvements resulting in improved performance 
 - Cubivore (Doubutsu Banchou w/English patch applied) support added

 - Added support for the Famicom data recorder
 - Added support for JY Company and SC-127 boards

armsx2.releaseNotes:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Library screensaver starts after 5 minutes by default
- Android tests: skip the stuck-file case where a folder cannot be made read-only (#906)
- Android: cite the malisx2 release, not the driver PR, in the offer comment
- Offer malisx2 on the Bifrost v7 parts it drives (Mali-G52, Mali-G76)
- What's new: reach the top with the pad, and outline the card itself
- What's new: let the pad read through an opened release
- What's new: show the pictures in release notes
- iOS: point the hack reason comment at the file with the enum
- iOS: apply turbo and slow motion speeds as saved
- iOS: reach the base settings only through Host's locked accessors
- iOS: split the bridge into one file per concern
- iOS: fail the build when a bridge method has no body
- VK: keep the feedback carry on PowerVR's in-tile road
- GS: recognise PowerVR CXT (Tensor G6) and size its pools
- VK: in-tile destination read on PowerVR without per-draw barriers
- VK: PowerVR self-reads through a subpass input attachment
- GL: PowerVR reads the destination through the ARM fetch builtin

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261029...cb78946d6ed0678b82fa3e0409c10124265ec18d

copperline_pc.releaseNotes:
Copperline 1.1.0 is the first feature release of the 1.x series. Hard drives can now run at the speed of the period drives each Amiga shipped with. The MMU-less 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060 are new CPU choices. The JIT is much faster on fast-RAM code and heavy disk I/O, and has a new "fastest" speed. A500 CIA, interrupt and bus timing are corrected against measurements of a real A500. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.0.1.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.1.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.0.x still load.** The CIA chunks are migrated to their new layout. A resumed 1.0.x state continues under the corrected timing, so it can drift from what 1.0.x would have produced (a factory A500 state from 1.0.1 still renders byte-identical frames). States saved by 1.1.0 do not load in 1.0.x, which reports that the state comes from a newer Copperline.
- **Emulated timing has moved.** The CIA, interrupt and bus corrections change when some events happen on every machine. Headless scripts and `--expect-screenshot` images tuned to an exact frame may need new timestamps or new captures.
- **A `copperline.toml` beside the executable now boots on its own.** Startup checks `--config`, then `./copperline.toml`, then a `copperline.toml` beside the executable (or beside `Copperline.app`, or beside the `.AppImage`), then the saved default. If you keep a file with that name there, it now takes over from the saved default. `--factory` skips it.
- **Relative media paths are also looked for in the `[paths]` media folders.** The working directory is still tried first, so every path that worked before finds the same file.
- **The bundled AROS ROM leaves 1,776 bytes less free memory** when a program starts.
- **Going back to 1.0.x:** 1.0.x refuses configuration files that use the new keys and values: `[cpu] speed`, the `68EC030`, `68EC040` and `68EC060` models, the drive `timing` and `spin_up` keys, and `[[drive_profile]]` tables.

## Period hard-drive timing

Until now every hard-disk transfer finished within the access that started it. `timing = "period"` on `[ide]`, `[scsi]` or `[lide]` (or `--hd-timing period`) models the drive each machine shipped with instead, so a hard-disk Amiga loads, boots and benchmarks at that drive's speed:

| Machine | Drive |
|---|---|
| A600 | Conner CP2024 |
| A1200 | Conner CP2064 |
| A4000 | Seagate ST3144A |
| A3000, and an A2091 in a big-box machine | Quantum LPS 52S |
| A590 | Seagate ST125N |
| A4091 | Seagate Hawk 1LP |
| lide boards | WD AC2120 |

The model covers command overhead, a seek curve fitted to each datasheet's track-to-track, average and full-stroke times, rotational latency from the platter's position, zoned media rates with track and cylinder skew, read-ahead, write caching, spin-up, standby and head parking. The 22 built-in profiles come from the manufacturers' manuals; `--list-drive-profiles` prints them, `timing` also takes a profile id, and `[[drive_profile]]` tables add your own, optionally based on a built-in one. `spin_up = true` also models the power-on spin-up. Each controller reports "not ready" the way its hardware does: IDE through BSY and DRQ, the WD33C93 (A2091, A590, A3000) through REQ, and the A4091's 53C710 by stalling its SCRIPTS processor. The launcher's Emulation page has Hard drive timing and Drive spin-up rows. The default stays `instant`, which behaves exactly as before. See [drive timing](https://copperline.dev/docs/configuration/#drive-timing).

## 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060

The three MMU-less "EC" parts are selectable as `[cpu] model` / `--cpu` and in the launcher. They keep their family's caches, stock clock and 32-bit bus, and each answers the MMU instructions as its silicon does: the 68EC030's access control unit (AC0, AC1, ACUSR and PTEST mat…

dsperate.releaseNotes:
# DSperate v3.3.0

GPU 3D update: a faster GPU raster, 4x MSAA back as the GPU raster's anti-aliasing with the edge cut moving to ENHANCED, and no more multi-second wait for the GPU raster to start.

## Features

- **Anti-aliasing on the GPU raster is 4x MSAA again; the edge cut is ENHANCED.** With `video.aa = true` (ON in the menu, `--aa`) the Vulkan GPU raster draws with 4x MSAA. The panel-density edge cut from v3.2.0, with texture cut-outs smoothed too, is now `video.aa = enhanced` (ENHANCED, `--aa-enhanced`). The cut is sharper, but on 3D-heavy games it costs the CPU more than MSAA costs the GPU (see Performance). On the CPU raster both settings are the hardware's own blend, as before. The OpenGL ES raster (the RG35XX SP) has no MSAA and no edge cut, so it draws without anti-aliasing.
- **Compiled GPU pipelines are kept between runs:** the Vulkan raster's and present's pipelines go to `vk_pipelines.bin` in `paths.cache` (default `~/.cache/dsperate/`), so after the first run, starting the GPU raster or switching between ON and ENHANCED takes milliseconds instead of a second and a half per mode. The unpacked-games cleanup never touches the file; `--clear-cache` deletes it. A driver update just rebuilds it.

## Performance

- **Faster GPU raster:** the DS's colour and texture-coordinate interpolation along each polygon row, which the GPU raster repeated exactly in integer maths, now runs in float. The difference from exact is a texel step landing a pixel early or late on 1–5 % of drawn pixels, which is not visible side by side; untextured polygons are unchanged. `DS_SPAN_EXACT=1` restores exact. RG DS Plus GPU time per frame, before → after:

  | | Pokémon White | SM64 DS | On Tour | Dragon Ball: Origins |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | no AA | 9.6 → 7.0 ms | 8.0 → 6.8 | 3.4 → 3.1 | 2.4 → 2.25 |
  | 4x MSAA | 17.8 → 10.4 ms | 22.6 → 12.1 | 6.8 → 4.9 | 3.8 → 3.4 |
  | edge cut | 10.5 → 7.8 ms | 10.4 → 8.9 | 5.3 → 4.9 | 2.9 → 2.8 |

  The OpenGL ES raster gets it too: Guitar Hero: On Tour on the RG35XX SP runs about 0.6 ms a frame faster.
- **Why the edge cut moved to ENHANCED:** its GPU frame is the cheaper one (Golden Sun: Dark Dawn, RG DS Plus: 8.3 ms against 10.3 for 4x MSAA), but its edge plane costs the emulation thread about 5 ms a frame there (21.3 ms median against 16.4), which a CPU-bound game feels more.
- **PGO profiles** refreshed for all four builds.

## Fixes

- **Edge cut start-up stall:** launching with ENHANCED built the GPU raster twice, the second time on the first frame (a ~7.6 s freeze). It is built once now, and from the pipeline cache.
- **Edge cut accuracy:** where two edges cross one pixel, the cut no longer depends on the order the polygons happened to be drawn in, so it stops flickering as the camera moves. A seam inside the scenery (a horizon, two faces of one hill) no longer cuts into whatever it runs into. Silhouettes keep their line where a seam meets them. Gaps and short hard seams along shallow edges are filled in, and a pixel squeezed between two lines facing each other stays whole. These mostly show along SM64 DS's hill crests against the sky and sea.
- **Settings and help text** corrected and clarified throughout (`--help`, the default ini, the README).

Full changelog: https://github.com/beebono/DSperate/compare/v3.2.0...v3.3.0

Games run without BIOS or firmware dumps (built-in FreeBIOS and a generated firmware); a set dumped from your own DS unlocks the firmware boot and cycle-exact SWI timing. None is included.

Tarballs: `linux-aarch64` is dynamically linked and stripped -- the one to package. `linux-aarch64-static` carries libstdc++/libgcc inside and keeps its debug symbols, for a device whose runtime is older than the build's, or for a backtrace.

freej2me_plus.releaseNotes:
# Happy Holidays, everyone!

Made an extra effort to finally finish two relatively lengthy commits in time for the holidays, so here it is: **V1.52**

It's a bit bigger release than 1.51 considering the changes, so here's the quick rundown:

- M3G should run noticeably faster than 1.51, and is slightly more compatible as well.
- FreeJ2ME-Plus now uses hand-written code for lcdui.Graphics rendering, allowing it to properly support DoJa's Graphics2 blending modes, and also fixing quite a few applications where Java AWT's usage caused issues (it now renders more accurate shapes as well).
- Many improvements to KDDI/ezPlus and DoJa, resulting in more compatible apps (some of these were done in tandem with the recent preservation work for ezPlus apps!)
- Many improvements to Nokia Sound, with its OTA tone decoder being near-perfectly accurate (can't support infinitely looping patterns, it's a MIDI limitation), and also faster compared to 1.51.
- lcdui.game classes (and Siemens equivalents) were cleaned up and now support transformed Sprite collisions, which should fix some games despite being a rather niche use case.
- A few LCDUI fixes in regards to form, list and command processing.
- Libretro fast-forward rate is now respected by the core (thanks to @Magstic)

## Pull Requests Merged
* fix: respect RetroArch fast-forward rate by @Magstic in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/171

## Full Changelog since v1.51: https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/compare/1.51...1.52

## _NOTE: As always, Libretro REQUIRES manually moving `freej2me-lr.jar` into the `system` folder, and `freej2me_libretro.(dll/so)` in the `cores` folder to work

# Now for the (potentially) less enticing news:

FreeJ2ME-Plus has some serious limitations as far as Libretro and TAS support are concerned. Its reliance on using the standard Java VM were a boon early on when the original authors worked on it, but with time (and especially now that i'm working more on stuff that goes outside the official MIDP-spec), i began to notice the pitfalls of that setup more and more.

- For libretro, it's impossible to have a properly functional core for it, since a bridge is required to connect the Java app to the C core (which at this point is little more than an image and input handler, audio is entirely handled by Java)

- For TAS, it's a lost cause given since the JVM likes to multithread as much as it can, and it was never conceived to work well in this environment, so timing issues are plenty, and even hurt some actual J2ME applications. In the future, it could be possible to make FreeJ2ME-Plus run on top of [SquirrelJME](https://github.com/SquirrelJME/SquirrelJME) which is much more portable and doesn't rely on the HotSpot VM, but that would require some decent refactoring in FJ2ME's code, and in that case, it's not worth it.

Tie those with the fact i already had to hand-write code to support graphics operations outside of Java AWT's scope, and i began to think i'm nearing a dead end, and could very well start programming something that doesn't rely on the Host's Java VM to run (and that could thus be more portable).

From now on, i'll be focusing far less in FreeJ2ME-Plus than before, as there's not much else to do that doesn't involve the massive 3D libraries, and continuing to work on these could very well end up being a fool's errand due to the limitations above.

### That doesn't mean i will stop developing for it, though

What this means, is that since [SquirrelJME](https://github.com/SquirrelJME/SquirrelJME) would be the "way out" for FreeJ2ME-Plus, i've decided "why not shift my focus to that instead?", and thus for the last few weeks, i've been far more active there than with FJ2ME+ itself and managed to push quite a few improvements. gse_speedrun.releaseNotes:
Sixth release of GSE.

This release replaces the GBA emulation core. Previously, [mGBA's](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba) GBA emulation core was used for GBA games. GSE now uses [Mesen's](https://github.com/nesdev-org/MesenCE) GBA emulation core for GBA games. This offers far better accuracy, to the point even GBA Pokémon TASes can sync on console, and as such emulator players can fairly compete with console players in GBA Pokémon speedrunners, along with likely many other games.

This release also features various bugfixes, along with minor QoL improvements such as an option to automatically hide the mouse cursor, saving the last used emulator width/height for when no ROM is loaded (i.e. no longer hardcoding GBA resolution), and more.

This release will likely be the last release for various old platforms (for macOS < 12, Linux < glibc 2.35, and Android < 7), mainly due to dependencies dropping support. This shouldn't affect most users, but it is noted for whatever users still use these old platforms.

Several download options are available, for various OSes and CPU architectures, per the [requirements listed in the README](https://github.com/CasualPokePlayer/GSE/blob/v0.6/README.md#user-requirements). For most users (with a Windows machine on an x64 device), the `GSE-win-x64.zip` file should be downloaded.

hakux.releaseNotes:
Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise
- **Morrowind** — no longer freezes when you leave a building: disc and hard-disk reads now take a little time, as on the console. The inventory's character is drawn properly: it no longer stands on red with a black band over its head, or leaves ghost copies of itself around it when you change gear after a load
- **Halo 2** — the fog no longer shows as stripes that move with the camera, and with the scope up the view around it is dimmed with black lines, not light blue
- **Munch's Oddysee** — no dark box over the ground under the characters' shadows
- **Project Zero II (PAL)** — no longer hangs on its first frame
- **Amped 2** — no longer crashes as its first level loads
- **Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks** — the models no longer explode on Mali-G57 GPUs
- **Burnout 2: Point of Impact** — no longer crashes as it starts
- **Def Jam: Fight for NY** — no longer freezes on one frame at the intro cutscene: while hakuX holds a game up (such as while its shaders compile), the game's clock now waits too
- **Double-S.T.E.A.L: The Second Clash** — no longer stops as its first scene begins, and the screen is no longer black, also after loading a savestate
- **Soldier of Fortune II: Double Helix** — no longer crashes when you skip an intro movie
- **Touge R** — races are no longer black under the HUD

### Performance
- **Network** — with the network on (system link or XLink Kai), the console no longer keeps most of a CPU core busy

### App
- **On-screen controls editor** — its toolbar wraps onto more rows on narrower screens, such as 4:3 handhelds, instead of pushing buttons off the edge

## Lemon-Project v1.3.0

Gamepad hotkeys, cheat downloads and a much steadier Quick Save/Load. Thanks again to **BitRanger** for seven more pull requests (GitHub #17 to #23), and welcome to Team Lemon!

### New
- **Gamepad hotkeys** (Settings → Controls → Hotkeys). Pick a Hotkey Enable button, then give each action the buttons to hold with it: Quick Save, Quick Load, show or hide the performance stats and the device info overlays, pause or unpause, and exit (it takes a second press unless "Confirm on Exit?" is turned off). As in RetroArch, Hotkey Enable is kept from the game while you use it: a quick tap of it still reaches the game, and so does holding it on its own. Hotkeys need a physical controller. (BitRanger)
- **Download cheats.** The Cheats window (game page or in-game menu) gets a Download button. It fetches the codes for your game's build from [switch-cheats-db](https://github.com/HamletDuFromage/switch-cheats-db), a database updated every day from gbatemp and NX-60FPS-RES-GFX-Cheats; all credit goes to the authors of the codes. Gameplay cheats and 60 FPS/resolution/graphics cheats go in their own folders, all off. Downloading again updates them and keeps the ones you turned on. Only the game's ID is sent, to GitHub.

### Quick Save/Load (BitRanger)
- **Loading across scenes no longer gives a black screen.** A state saved on a title screen and loaded after starting a run came back black while the game ran on. A load now drops what the GPU drew since the save and puts the GPU engines' state back as it was.
- **"Game is busy" much less often.** The audio kept waking the game's audio thread while it was paused for a save, so a save kept looking for a quiet moment, with the sound stuttering. The audio is now held while a save or a load runs.
- A load no longer overwrites a service's answer that arrived while the game was paused for it (the game aborted with 2010-0212 right after the load), and no longer matches a thread back from a different kernel call (2001-0117).
- Messages replace each other instead of queueing: "Saving…"/"Loading…" stay until the result, with "still processing…" for a long one.

### Fixed
- A thread whose first run was cut short could start with a TLS address of 0, and the game then closed. (BitRanger)
- Monster Hunter Generations Ultimate online on Nextendo Network: two friend service requests it makes (the friend list IDs and the online session declaration) now get an answer instead of none.
- Saving the settings no longer logs a critical error when a game has several add-ons turned off.

### Install
Android 12 or newer, arm64. Signed with Lemon's key, like 1.2.2: it updates in place and keeps your data.
`Lemon-v1.3.0-standard.apk` · `Lemon-Lite-v1.3.0-lite.apk` · `Lemon-Lite-Spoofed-v1.3.0-lite-spoofed.apk`

### Nuevo
- **Atajos del mando** (Ajustes → Controles → Atajos del mando). Elige un botón de atajos y asigna a cada acción los botones que se pulsan con él: guardado rápido, carga rápida, mostrar u ocultar las estadísticas de rendimiento y la información del dispositivo, pausar o reanudar, y salir (pide una segunda pulsación salvo que desactives "¿Confirmar al salir?"). mame4droid.releaseNotes:
#  Rollback NetPlay: compatibility and stability

Rollback is what makes NetPlay feel like two people on one machine instead of
two people waiting for each other. This release is mostly about the games that
could not use it, and the sessions that fell apart halfway through.

## Street Fighter III now runs in rollback

All of CPS-3 does: 3rd Strike and the earlier two, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure,
Red Earth. Until now these were stuck in Lockstep, which is the worst place for
a fighting game to be.

The problem was size. To rewind, rollback keeps dozens of snapshots of the
machine in memory, and a CPS-3 snapshot was enormous — it carried the entire
game loaded from the CD, tens of megabytes of code, graphics and samples that
never change while you play. Snapshots now leave all of that behind and keep
only what the game actually writes to. What used to be far past any sane limit
now fits with room to spare.

Games that already fit benefit too: smaller snapshots mean less memory and less
work on every correction.

## More games run in rollback

The host now hands its machine state to the joiner by default, so games that
used to refuse rollback because both sides could not be trusted to boot
identically now qualify.

## Sessions that used to break

**Joining and resyncing.** A drop-in join or a mid-game resync would sometimes
leave one machine frozen, or the joiner on a black screen, with nothing to do
but disconnect. The snapshot was being taken wherever the emulation happened to
be at that instant, sometimes in the middle of a frame with work still pending.
It is now always taken at the end of a frame, once the video chip has finished
and the interrupt queue is drained. The state that arrives is one the other
machine can actually resume from.

**Brief network drops.** Lose enough packets in a row and one frame would stay
a guess forever: the game kept running, quietly wrong, and the two sides drifted
apart over the next minutes. That frame is now re-requested from the other
player and the session repairs itself. Tested by cutting the connection on
purpose, over and over.

**Dials, spinners and 4-way sticks.** Part of the live control state was not
included in a rollback, so analog games could jump or fall back to a stale
reading after a correction. It travels with the state now.

## Quick messages

The last release said there would be no chat, and there still isn't one. What
there is now is a short list of fixed phrases — hello, good game, wait a moment,
insert coin and press start, I have to go. Picking one sends a number, not text,
and the other player's device shows that phrase in their own language. Nothing
typed, nothing to moderate, nothing stored. You can mute the ones you receive.

## Drop-in BIOS selection

For games with several BIOS versions, the picker was starting on an arbitrary
one and, if you pressed Exit instead of choosing, it published your room anyway.
It now starts on the game's default BIOS, and Exit cancels the whole thing.

## Smaller things

- Dialogs start with a sensible button selected, so a gamepad can go through
  NetPlay without touching the screen. Disconnect is never the one selected,
  and it now sits at the bottom of the menu, away from the rest.
- The public room board shows the busiest countries on a line of its own.

## Both devices must be updated

The network protocol changed. An updated device and an old one will refuse each
other when connecting, which is deliberate: the alternative is a session that
looks fine and slowly falls apart.

This release brings a large collection of game compatibility and graphics fixes, more flexible controls, audio improvements, and easier management of save states and DSi configurations. --- ## Controls and Gameplay ### Optional Vulkan low-latency mode A new optional Vulkan mode improves touch responsiveness, including in affected gameplay scenarios in **The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass**. This can make touch-driven gameplay feel more responsive, but enabling it may reduce smoothness in demanding games. **It is disabled by default.** ### Multitouch fixes Holding one virtual button while pressing another now works correctly. This fixes combinations such as holding **Y** to run while pressing **B** to jump. Related issue: [#132](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/issues/132). ### Better controller behavior - Fixed controllers becoming unresponsive after returning from per-game settings or rewind. - Fixed a white overlay appearing when clicking a stick without an assigned action. Each button supports pressed-state highlighting and **Normal**, **Toggle**, and **Turbo** modes. **Existing layouts are preserved.** Related: [#158](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/issues/158), [#191](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/issues/191), [Discussion #178](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/discussions/178). ### More flexible shortcuts New shortcut options let you: - Cycle between layouts you have selected. - Exit the current game. - Assign combinations of two physical controller buttons. **Note:** The first button in a combination can also trigger its individual action. Related: [Discussion #175](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/discussions/175), [Discussion #161](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/discussions/161). ### Virtual Slot-2 analog stick A virtual Slot-2 stick provides analog input for games or mods that support the corresponding accessory. **This does not add analog controls to every Nintendo DS game.** Related: [Discussion #167](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/discussions/167). ### Rotation, pause, and resume fixes Fixed image distortion when rotating the screen with Vulkan, and an OpenGL crash that could occur when pausing or resuming. mz800emu_pc.releaseNotes:
- BUGFIX: Sound - a PSG channel that changed exactly at the start of an audio frame was held at its previous level for the whole frame (20 ms, on the MZ-1500 16.7 ms) in the sound output, in music once every one to three seconds; usually not audible in music, clearly visible when comparing with the exact sound of the audio capture (reference.wav). The sound recorded into a video in emulated time did not have this defect.

- Audio capture in the GUI and on the command line: Tools -> Audio Capture -> Record Audio Capture (Alt+Q) records into a new folder in its own output folder (default audio_captures next to the emulator) what the sound hardware does - changes of the channel levels, PSG writes, the exact sound and the sound you hear (two WAV files to compare); AUDIO with the captured time is shown in the top left corner of the picture, a notification reports the folder. Settings... sets the output folder and selects the files to write. --audio-capture <folder> starts it right after startup, --audio-capture-frames <count> stops it after the given number of frames (with --headless the emulator then exits). See audio-capture.md.

- MCP - audio capture for finding sound bugs: emu_audio_capture_start writes into a folder, in emulated time, every change of the output level of the sound channels (speaker and PSG channels, events.csv), every write to the PSG with its decoding (psg_writes.csv), the sound rendered exactly in emulated time (reference.wav) and the sound of the emulator's audio output path, i.e. what the user hears (sdl.wav, same format for a direct comparison); capture.json describes the capture. emu_audio_capture_stop and emu_audio_capture_status. See mcp-server/tools-overview.md.

- Debugger - the CPU Profiler window has a new Per PC tab: for every instruction address it counts executions, T-states (including wait states) and WAIT states, also in code that is jumped to rather than called. Columns can be sorted, a range of addresses can be shown, a left click opens the address in the Disassembly; the status line splits the time into instructions, waiting in HALT and the rest (mainly interrupt acknowledge). Export CSV writes all addresses. See debugger/profiler.md.

- MCP - per-PC profiler for finding where a program spends its time: emu_profiler_pc_start, emu_profiler_pc_stop, emu_profiler_pc_reset, emu_profiler_pc_get (busiest addresses with the nearest symbol, sorted by T-states, executions, WAIT or address, optional address range) and emu_profiler_pc_export (CSV). Time outside instructions is reported separately (halt_idle, other_tstates). With the profiler off the emulation is not slowed down. See mcp-server/tools-overview.md.

- Frame series in the GUI: Tools -> Screenshot -> Record Changed Frames (Alt+Shift+F) saves a PNG of every emulated frame that differs from the previous one (or of every frame, see Settings...) into a new folder in the screenshot output folder, with the area and scale from the screenshot settings. A counter in the top left corner of the picture shows the saved files and frames; a notification reports the folder when the series ends. See screenshots.md.

- MCP - frame series for finding animation bugs: emu_screenshot_series_start saves a PNG of every emulated frame that differs from the last saved one (or of every frame), with the same area, scale and crop as a single screenshot; only changes inside them count. Frames are taken in emulated time, none is skipped even at MAX SPEED (the emulation waits when writing cannot keep up). Files frame_NNNNNNN.png numbered by the emulated frame and index.csv; emu_screenshot_series_stop and emu_screenshot_series_status. See mcp-server/headless-mode.md.

- New feature: screenshots (Tools -> Screenshot) on all platforms. Save Screenshot (Alt+F) saves a PNG of the picture shown in the window into the output folder (default: screenshots next to the emulator) with a name made of the platform and time, Save Screenshot As... asks for the file name.…

Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays and a Happy New Year everyone!

This update adds experimental Online Multiplayer to NetherSX2 along with the usual updates!
Thanks to [IamLupo](https://github.com/IamLupo) for adding it to ARMSX2, and [zakilj3](https://www.youtube.com/user/zakilj3) for discovering the same settings work with NetherSX2!

[VirusTotal Scan Report](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/8b502b31ce797d5a162bc6b9300b5f02351b0b6b290b8dc1390b8dfb826673ab)

## How to use Online Multiplayer
1. Go to your App Settings --> Settings and toggle on Enable DEV9 Ethernet
2. Set API to Sockets, and Device to how you want to connect online with the default being WiFi. Set this to VPN if your phone uses a VPN, and to one of the two SIM DATA options if you want to use your Mobile Data Plan instead
3. That should be enough to get you online using a guide like [this](https://youtu.be/dcOnZzzcbSc?si=WOf01r0Ln5ZVQkpf&t=278) by LogicalMacrochip

You can use the [Official List of PlayStation 2 Online Games (2024)](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15pfhL36qmC-iKr8MNjNXNLwgacG4VOmkfvwVxV5vGzo/edit?gid=0#gid=0) to figure out what games work, get their DNAS bypass codes if needed and which private server you should be using

# v26500801 — Gameplay background-work preview

This update removes unnecessary work during ordinary gameplay with frame generation off. It keeps the Classic 3668 core, driver selection, game patches and saved settings from v26500800.

- Turning framegen off now removes its overlay and stops its twice-per-second monitor. A cold start with framegen off does not start that monitor. Enabling framegen and resolution-change recovery still start it when needed.
- Returning to a game applies OSD settings once. Later recovery checks only reload settings if the native emulator has actually changed the OSD preferences or an earlier apply failed. Older resume callbacks cannot apply settings in a newer session.
- FPS visibility and the user's all-stats-off choice remain supported. Flow stays 0.25 and artifact protection stays off. Framegen remains available on 60 Hz displays; this update does not change its saved switch position.

Install either APK over the existing Pink app without uninstalling or clearing data. FRAMEGEN and NONFRAMEGEN share the same package, signing certificate, memory cards and save states. The Daijisho connector from v26500800 remains compatible.

Automated checks cover monitor shutdown/re-enable, resolution recovery, redundant reload prevention, failed-apply retries and OSD preference repair. Both APKs pass signing, package/version, icon, settings layout and variant checks. The emulator core and FRAMEGEN LSFG library are byte-identical to v26500800.

This is a preview of specific background-work fixes, not a universal locked-60 claim. Game caps, patch compatibility, CPU/GPU load and storage activity still affect performance. Physical checks and measurement limits are recorded in the accompanying validation receipt.

On Nova, Ultimate Spider-Man launched from Daijisho with framegen off. Resolution changes in both 4:3 and widescreen, FPS ON/OFF, and restoring the current session passed. All eight existing save/card files and seven backed-up configuration files remained byte-identical; the current session was preserved in one previously empty save slot.

The initial widescreen camera-pan sample reported about 59.94 game FPS and two roughly 33 ms presentation intervals across 44 seconds, while a large SD-card transfer was active. These initial samples do not establish a clean before/after performance improvement.

Follow-up tests briefly paused the transfer and resumed it safely after each comparison. Hitches also occurred without the transfer. With framegen off, the best longer Nova sample used Sync To Host Refresh Rate, Host VSync and Threaded Presentation together: one 33.36 ms presentation interval across 109.28 seconds of camera movement in Ultimate Spider-Man at 1.5x and 4:3. Those timing settings were retained on the test Nova. A shorter zero-outlier result did not hold across longer tests, so occasional hitches remain and locked 60 is not verified. This follow-up changes only the test device settings and validation notes; the APKs and shipped defaults are unchanged. Thor, other games and sustained city traversal were not retested.

See the [validation receipt](https://github.com/slushiimusic/NetherSX2-Slushii-Turnip-Fix/blob/main/releases/v26500801-validation.json) for the sample metrics and scope.

nuance_pc.releaseNotes:
- FINALLY, T3K can be played with no hangs on music transitions, and with proper music looping!
  Also the level select hang (with DynamicCompiler enabled) is resolved (see GameCompatibility.txt/MPE3PacketHack-option though for the caveats)!
- Merlin Racing's AI drivers now follow the course as intended (with DynamicCompiler enabled).
- Add Linux port with CMake build system, X11/GLX backend and miniaudio audio output.
- Add libretro port.
- 32-bit build supports the x86 JIT dynamic recompiler on Linux via `__attribute__((fastcall))`.
- 64-bit builds employ asmjit instead.
- Static linking of glew (no more `glew32.dll` needed).
- Replace FMOD 3.75 with miniaudio. No more outdated FMOD SDK / `fmod.dll` dependency.
- Due to this, decouple host audio from Nuon DMA via a ring buffer (which was implicitly done by FMOD under the hood).
- Audio interrupts are kept intact while muted (matches previous behavior, needs to be verified on real HW).
- Drag and drop support for the UI.
- Can load games directly from ZIP/ISO files on Windows.
- On Linux additionally supports RAR/7z via FUSE tools.
- All "with carry" opcodes (=addwc/subwc/cmpwc variants) should now behave as written in the ISA spec.
- MSB JIT bug fixed.
- Fix bug in JIT versions of MULScalarShiftAcshift, MULImmediateShiftAcshift, MULScalarShiftScalar and MULImmediateShiftScalar (shift broken if left shift >= 32 used).
- Fix bug in JIT version of MULImmediateShiftLeftImmediate (wrong dependency used).
- Fix bug in ANDImmediateShiftScalar, ANDScalarShiftScalar, FTSTImmediateShiftScalar, FTSTScalarShiftScalar, ORImmediateShiftScalar, ORScalarShiftScalar, EORImmediateShiftScalar, EORScalarShiftScalar (shift broken if left shift == 32 used).
- Fix wrong flag setting for large numbers (highest bit set) in JIT versions of DECRc0 and DECRc1.
- Fix missing JIT implementations for loading odmactl,odmacptr,mdmactl,mdmacptr,comminfo,commctl,commxmit0/1/2/3,commrecv0/1/2/3 and configa/configb/dcachectl/icachectl.
- BTST is still not same as ISA spec (as apparently a real HW bug, at least on Aries 2 (=tested there)).
- Multiple bugs in the "CompilerConstantPropagation"-enabled path fixed, so enabled by default now, leading to more performance.
- Fix "_MPEAlloc()" logic to match original BIOS.
- Correct Audio Buffer sizes used for all configurations (via GetBufferSize()).
- Unfortunately, Tetris now sounds even worse than before.
- Fix (re)loading of 2ndary games: reset audio + MPE states.
- To make (at least) T3K work better, the whole MediaRead (and partially MediaWrite) implementation has been redone
  to better match the spec (incl. proper return values, proper callback mode handling, and not filling up buffers too early),
  at the tradeoff that now the loads actually need some time to arrive (incl. potential stutter).
- Fix "_MediaGetInfo()" byte-swapped fields.
- Fix uninitialized framebuffer (e.g. when starting fullscreen from command line).
- Optimize most JIT code that needs to do bswap/endian change.
- Enforce rz/rzi1/rzi2 (matching the Nuon hardware) to have bit 0 as 0 (due to 16-bit alignment).
- Some JIT instructions now are implemented correctly on non-SSE4.1 capable hardware (MUL_SVScalarShiftSvshift, MUL_SVRuShiftSvshift and MUL_SVRvShiftSvshift had vector-lane swaps for 2 components).
- Fix JIT for PVectorShiftSvshift (had wrong z component).
- Handle ITAGS and CTRL tags correctly in the JIT versions of StoreScalarLinear & StoreVectorLinear.
- Handle vdma* loads in JIT.
- Fix a potential correctness issue in the JIT MULScalarShiftLeftImmediate and MULImmediateShiftLeftImmediate with shifts > 32.
- Fix JIT RangeOnly and ModuloOnly register indices.
- instructiontest.cof has been updated with more tests (verified to match real HW / Samsung DVD-N501).

Release Notes for openMSX 22.0 (2026-10-28)
===========================================

Thanks to many contributors (who make good use of modern AI tools), we
have a very long list of changes again. Major features are found in the
debugger GUI, with a new Raster Beam Viewer and Tracer functionality. We also
have the Quick Setup Editor, for one-window access to all major setup
settings.

Then AI hit us with dozens of Pull Requests with new and improved
functionality... Not all purely AI-generated, but also using AI to analyse
bulk measurements. This led to many VDP accuracy improvements and emulation of
new devices like plotters, Panasonic FS-JH1 Joy Handle steering wheel (that
came with Konami's A1 Spirit), light guns, Franky, Makoto, SD Mapper V1 and
SM-X WiFi. There's even a synthetic TCP/IP UNAPI device to be able to try out
network programs in openMSX.

And many, many more things...

Special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core
team! Keep those pull requests coming!

Here's the list with all highlights and details:

MSX device support:
- fixed Yamanooto SCC register visibility
- added emulation of the Sony PRN-C41 (like) plotters, including a viewer in the
  GUI
- fixed details on the turboR's FDC emulation, so that now FastCopy 3.0
  properly detects it, including the correct number of drives
- added MSX Light Gun emulation, controlled with the mouse on the host:
  - MHT GUN-STICK
  - ASCII Plus-X Terminator Laser
- added Korean 128-in-1 mapper type
- added Namco mapper type (A13-not-connected 16kB cartridges)
- added ASCII8-R (reversed) mapper type
- fixed details of MSX kanji ROM emulation, adding specific behaviour in many
  machines and devices
- added Panasonic FS-JH1 Joy Handle (belongs with Konami's A1 Spirit),
  including configuration window
- added SuperSoniqs Franky emulation (allows playing Sega Master System games
  on MSX)
- added SuperSoniqs Makoto emulation (OPNA sound cartridge)
- added SD Mapper V1 emulation
- added SM-X WiFi emulation (UNAPI compatible ESP WiFi module), connecting
  either to a real ESP32 on a host serial port or to an emulated one that uses
  the host network
- updated Neo mapper support to specification version 1.2, now using 14 bits
  of the segment register (up to 16384 segments)
- VDP:
  - fixed VDP I/O delay to 1 cycle for machines with a T9769 MSX-ENGINE (all
    subtypes)
  - added implementation of the TEXT2-mode per line blink (bit 2 in VDP R#2)
  - improved timing correctness of the YMMM and LMMM commands
  - several other VDP command timing improvements (including start delays)
  - improved VDP-VRAM timing even further
  - fixed display line counter latch (fixes Sex Bomb Bunny shaking screen)
  - fixed border color changes at the wrong position (last part of Utopia)
  - fixed wrong location for sprite collision flag raising, causing distorted
    MSX2+ logo animation
  - fixed 5th/9th sprite flag raise location, obsoleting the special openMSX
    workaround in the IO demo
  - fixed wrong location of application of R#23 changes (8-pixel boundary)
  - fixed: ignore the TP bit in text, multicolor and YAE modes
- PSG:
  - assume that no PSG implementation mirrors its registers (no evidence found
    they do so far...)
  - fixed interpretation of envelope period of 0 (same as 1)
  - fixed: do not reset the envelope index when writing the envelope shape
    register

# 2.6.2

Fixes for the themes, the update notifier, Exceptions, the Legendary parser and importing artwork choices.

## Easier to see in every theme

Buttons, switches and games without artwork used to almost disappear in themes whose colors are close together, such as Solarized Light, Mint and Pride. They now stand out in every theme, including themes you made yourself. The text in input bubbles (for example "Global" under User accounts) can be read in light themes too.

## Update download progress

Downloading an update now shows a progress bar with the size and download speed. It updates by itself; before, the progress only changed when you moved the mouse.

Also:

- If a download fails, SRM says so, with a link to the release on GitHub. Before, the progress stopped and nothing else happened.
- Downloading again after cancelling a download works.
- When the update is downloaded you can choose No as well as Restart.

## Fixes

- **Saving exceptions no longer fails with "must be string"** after deleting an exception.
- **Legendary games launch again** when SRM finds Legendary by itself ([#719](https://github.com/SteamGridDB/steam-rom-manager/issues/719)). The path it found ended with a line break, which broke the shortcut. Also, if Legendary isn't installed, the parser now says so instead of never finishing, and finding it no longer needs PowerShell 7.
- **Importing artwork choices counts only the games in the list** ([#724](https://github.com/SteamGridDB/steam-rom-manager/issues/724)). Games that are no longer installed are skipped, and the log names them.

## Other changes

- SRM's license is now stated as GPL-3.0-or-later ([#882](https://github.com/SteamGridDB/steam-rom-manager/issues/882)).
- Updated dependencies, including security fixes.

Hello!

It's been a little while, so I thought I would just give a small update on project status. 

- Winlator Cmod development continues!
- My focus on next release will either be mostly QoL. This means addressing long standing bug fixes, but more importantly, **merging and crediting improvements from other forks of Cmod from trusted developers.** Primarily I'll be focused on:
- Fixing dynamic package name paths for the gamepad implementation so that name can be changed, such as adding a ludashi benchmark version with the SDL joystick native controller support.
- Input control / touch screen control bindings bug fixes
- Minor UI improvements and enhancements
- Updating all drivers, Fex, Box64, and graphics Wrapper, following Pipetto-Crypto's advice when it comes to Streamlining and avoiding feature creep (...and avoiding pure AI code slop). 
- Improve ALSA-Reflector so audio stops cutting out after 15 minutes unless you switch to headphones.

I'm leaning on this being v13.2. A v14 Cmod should be more substantial. Ultimately I would like to overhaul how Containers are created, with a focus on something more aligned and user friendly like Gamehub, such as starting the app and choosing a Windows based executable directly in the UI, then auto creating or maintain a single container or edge case containers. This would work well with something like Per Game Fixes, or a standardized compatibility list like what's on Reddit.  

Lastly, I'm sorry I'm not good about addressing Github issues. I just have not had any time. However, it is all incredibly helpful for me; the time that I do have to spend on the next release and addressing what issues have been posted this past year (...and _cough_ Arc _cough_ raiding...). I am also looking forward to what Valve brings to the table with the Frame and it's ARM based Linux OS with Android app support. I imagine Proton is going to be getting some major improvements for ARM over the next year, so I don't see things slowing down much. Google seems to be walking back some of the unknown app restrictions they announced this year, so that's also good. Lots to look forward to. 

Stay Kazzy,
Goro Majima

# X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 2

This update brings general correctness, graphics, stability and efficiency improvements, developed and evaluated using **Split/Second** as a reference game. These are improvements to the emulator itself rather than fixes restricted to one title. Other games may also benefit, but broader compatibility and performance testing is still limited.

## Improvements

- Improved handling of demanding graphics workloads and reduced avoidable processing overhead.
- Corrected visual consistency and resource-handling issues, including an issue affecting frame interpolation.
- Improved the reliability of the touch-control layout editor.
- Added optional independent auto-hide for the Menu button.
- Reorganized Settings with fewer main categories and clearer access to game content, patches and advanced tools.

## Split/Second: still experimental

On the tested **Snapdragon 8 Gen 2** setup, Split/Second currently fluctuates around **8–18 FPS**, depending on the scene and the selected experimental settings. The game **still requires extensive further work to become playable on this SoC**. Occasional pauses and remaining graphical issues are still under investigation.

The experimental per-game options used for these tests remain **opt-in**; this update does not enable them globally. Results on other devices, drivers and games have not been widely verified.

## Updating

- Public version **0.6.4 Hotfix 2**, build **60411113**. Existing installations can update in place and keep their games, settings and saves.
- Includes the fixes from Hotfix 1. TV mode and synchronized player profiles remain highly experimental.
- X360 Companion is unchanged.
